courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
courses.description: The correlation of mechanical properties with atomic bonding, microstructure, and micromechanics, for applications relevant to materials selection and design, mechanical forming, and failure of materials.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Materials Laboratory I
courses.description: Characterization of engineering properties of materials through hands-on experiments. Instruction on basic laboratory skills, safety, statistical analysis of data, use of laboratory notebooks and technical report writing.

courses.title: Transport Phenomena

courses.title: Polymer and Fiber Processing
courses.description: Discussion of the principles of fiber formation from polymers including rheology, mechanics, energetics, phase transition, and polymer structure. High-performing fiber processing, and plastics processing. Credit not allowed for both MSE 3230 and PTFE 3230.

courses.title: Introduction to Polymer/Fiber Enterprise
courses.description: Approaches the manufacture of engineered fibrous structures from a manager's viewpoint and gives a working knowledge and understanding of various processes used in producing polymers/fibers/fiber products. Restricted to non-MSE majors. Credit not allowed for MSE 3720.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Ceramic Materials: Properties, Processing, Applications
courses.description: Properties, processing, and applications of the industrially and technically important ceramic materials. Traditional and oxide ceramics in addition to glass and nonoxide ceramics.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Materials in Electronic Applications
courses.description: Basics of photolithography, screen printing, and tape casting. Requirements for fuel cells, magnetic nanocomposites, flat-panel displays, gas sensors, piezoelectric acutators, photonic crystals, etc.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Processing and Applications of Engineering Alloys
courses.description: Solidification, deformation, and powder processing of metals and alloy;, microstructural design at nano- and meso-length scales; and structure-property correlations.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Environmental Degradation
courses.description: Theory of environmental degradation of metals, ceramics, polymers, and biomaterials. Emphasis on the scientific principles of corrosion and physical degradation.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Materials Laboratory II
courses.description: Processing, structure, properties relationships are explored through a series of hands-on experiments. Instruction on basic laboratory skills, safety, statistical analysis of data, use of laboratory notebooks and technical report writing.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSE 2021 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fiber Product Manufacturing
courses.description: The manufacture of fiber products and their process- structure-property relationships are detailed, covering fibers, yarns, fabrics, nonwovens, carpets, composites, and related materials.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Deformation and Fracture of Materials
courses.description: Deformation and fracture of metals, ceramics, polymers and composites for applications relevant to material selection and design, mechanical forming processes, and analysis of engineering failures.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymer Physics
courses.description: Physical chemistry of polymer solutions, polymer miscibility, adsorptions, sorptions, plasticization, molecular weights, molecular weight distributions. Study of polymer surfaces. Credit not allowed for MSE 4140.

courses.description: Introduction to industrial controls in manufacturing, process modeling, control of continuous-variable processes, digital control, discrete control, and control of manufacturing systems.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Capstone Design
courses.description: Seniors will work in teams to apply a systematic design process to real multi-disciplinary problems. Problems selected from a broad spectrum of interest areas, including biomedical, environmental, mechanical, industrial design, electrical and thermal/fluids. Projects must be based on the knowledge and skills acquired in earlier course work, and incorporate appropriate engineering standards and multiple realistic constraints. Emphasis is placed on the design process, the technical aspects of the design, and on reducing the proposed design to practice. The course consists of faculty and guest lectures, prototyping in design studios, and a multi-disciplinary design project.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Functional Materials
courses.description: This course focuses on the effects of defects on physical properties; charge/mass transport; semiconductors, heterojunctions, electrical and magnetic polarization, interaction processes between various physical properties; electrical characterization techniques.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Transmission Electron Microscopy
courses.description: Introduction to the kinematical electron scattering theory, optics in TEM, diffraction contrast imaging of defects, dynamical electron diffraction effects; and chemical microanalysis using EDS.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Quantitative Characterization of Microstructures
courses.description: Application of statistically unbiased methods for estimating geometrical attributes of microstructures and nonplanar fracture surfaces from plane sections and projections, digital image analysis, and computer simulations of microstructures.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Surface Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to vacuum science and technology; structure of solid surfaces; electron and ion energy analyzers, electron spectroscopies (e.g., AES and XPS); ion-based techniques (e.g., SIMS and RBS); depth profiling; ion channeling.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Computational Materials Science and Engineering
courses.description: This course aims to provide a broad understanding of a spectrum of modern state-of-the-art computational methods used in materials science and engineering.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Defects
courses.description: Emphasis on the origin and character of point, line, and surface defects in crystalline materials and their influence on mechanical, chemical, magnetic, optical, and electronic properties.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Materials for Energy Storage and Conversion
courses.description: Scientific principles concerning the transfer, capture, and storage of energy harnessed from various sources, including solar, wind, geothermal, and biomass.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Soft Nanomaterials and Nanostructures
courses.description: Fundamentals and applications of soft (polymer and biological) nanomaterials such as colloidal assemblies, self-assembled structures, energy devices, photonic materials, drug delivery, flexible electronics, soft robotics.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
courses.description: To examine the principles of thermodynamics as applied to equilibria associated with solutions, mixtures, chemical reactions, and interfaces in materials.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Crystallography, Structure and Defects
courses.description: Provides students with a fundamental understanding of crystal structures, symmetry, origin, character, defects in crystalline materials, and the influence of these defects on different properties.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Kinetics of Phase Transformations
courses.description: To introduce the fundamentals of thermodynamics and mathematics to the kinetics of diffusional and non-diffusional phase transformation in engineering materials.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Scattering Theory
courses.description: A general introduction to the scattering/diffraction of electromagnetic radiation from solids. The kinematical formalism is developed emphasizing x-ray scattering as a characterization tool.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Nanomaterials
courses.description: Topics include the synthesis and growth processes controlling quantum dot formation, nanowires, and three- dimensional self-assembled nanostructures. Additional characterization techniques and emerging applications are presented.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Corrosion of Materials
courses.description: To introduce students to the basic kinetic mechanisms associated with the interactions of materials with liquids and gases.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics - MSE
courses.description: Fundamental of quantum mechanics of atoms, molecules and solids necessary for engineers to understand the electronic, optical and thermal properties of inorganic and organic materials.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Corrosion
courses.description: Course covers thermodynamics, and kinetics of metallic corrosion in electrolytes and high-temperature oxidation. Different forms of corrosion, their mechanisms, and corrosion control methods are discussed.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
courses.description: This course introduces structural features of materials, including point/space groups, representative crystal structures, quasi-crystals, amorphous and rubbery state, liquid crystals, colloids, solutions, and effect of symmetry on properties.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Structure of Materials
courses.description: This course introduces structural features of materials, including point/space groups, representative crystal structures, quasi-crystals, amorphous and rubbery state, liquid crystals, colloids, solutions, and effect of symmetry on properties.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymers for Electronic and Photonic Applications I
courses.description: Review of fundamentals and principles of polymers used in electronics and photonics; relationships between the advances of semiconductor technology and the importance of polymers and their applications.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Polymer Processing
courses.description: Common polymer processing techniques and recent advancement; Modeling of polymer processing focusing on how to build a sound model; Computer aided engineering for polymer processing.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Natural Polymers
courses.description: The structures and properties of natural products are presented. Production of cellulose and proteins in discussed. Credit not allowed for both MSE 6603 and PTFE 6301.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Materials Science of Cellular Components
courses.description: Addresses structure-property relationship of cellular components. Credit not allowed for both MSE 6730 and BMED 6730.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Preparation & Reactions of Polymers
courses.description: A detailed treatment of the reactions involved in the synthesis of both human-made and natural polymers, including preparation and degradative reactions of polymer systems.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Physical Chemistry of Polymer Solutions
courses.description: Study of polymer solutions, polymer miscibility, adsorption, sorptions, plasticization, molecular weights, molecular weight distribution, and interfacial phenomena using thermodynamics and statistical mechanics. Crosslisted with CHEM, CHE, and PTFE 6751.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymer Characterization
courses.description: This course introduces the student to surface, near-surface and structural methods of polymer characterization. Specialized techniques critical to physical structure are emphasized. Crosslisted with CHEM, CHE, and PTFE 6752.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Engineering Communication
courses.description: Writing and editing engineering documents; designing and explaining visuals; creating and delivering electronic presentations. Crosslisted with CEE 6754.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Theoretical Chemistry of Polymers
courses.description: Thermodynamics and microscopic dynamics of polymers. Fundamental concepts, including scaling concepts, governing anisotropy of polarizability, phase transitions, morphology, time-dependent correlations, etc. are discussed. Crosslisted with CHEM and PTFE 6755.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Polymer Chemistry
courses.description: Advanced topics in synthetic polymerization methodology, polymer structure, and polymer properties in solution and the solid state.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymer Structure, Physical Properties, and Characterization
courses.description: Formulations and analysis of molecular and phenomenological models of elastic and viscoelastic behavior, development and description of structure, and fundamental aspects of structure-property relations. Crosslisted with TFE, CHE, and ME 6768.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymer Communications
courses.description: Oral and written presentation of modern polymer topics, with an emphasis on constructive and ethical critical thinking in a group setting.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Integrated Low-cost Microelectronics Systems Packaging
courses.description: Broad overview of system-level, cross-disciplinary microelectronics packaging technologies, including design, test, thermal, reliability, optoelectronics, and RF integration. Comparison of system-to-chip and system-to-package. Crosslisted with ECE and ME 6776.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Biomaterials
courses.description: Advanced topics of biomaterials performance and engineering, including biointerfaces, host reactions to materials, and bio-inspired/smart-materials strategies. Crosslisted with BMED, CHE, and ME 6777.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Mathematical, Statistical, and Computational Techniques in Materials Science
courses.description: Fundamental physical, analytical, and mathematical techniques encountered in materials engineering including stress and strain, crystallographic and orientation transformations, X-ray, TEM, and solid-state concepts are emphasized. Crosslisted with ME and PTFE 6795.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Structure-Property Relationships in Materials
courses.description: Introduction to the multi-scale structure effects on material properties. Course will prepare students for future in-depth courses. Crosslisted with PTFE and ME 6796.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Electroceramics
courses.description: Defects chemistry; electrochemical and electrophysical behavior of metallic/semiconducting ceramics, dielectrics, and ferrites; device applications of various electronic ceramics.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Impedance and Dielectric Spectroscopy
courses.description: The basic theory of how current, voltage, and phase angle measurements over a wide frequency range (typically mHz-MHz) can provide information about microstructural features at all length scales.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Dislocation and Deformation Mechanics
courses.description: Emphasis on interactions of dislocations with other defects, dislocation dynamics, and their correlation with mechanical properties under different rates of loading.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Solidification Processing
courses.description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics, kinetics, mass transport, and physical materials are applied to the development of microstructure during solidification.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymers for Electronic and Photonic Applications II
courses.description: Review of fundamentals and principles of polymers used in electronics and photonics. The relationship between the recent advances of semiconductor technology and the importance of polymers will be discussed.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Teaching Practicum
courses.description: Students will learn about what it takes to be a faculty through sills needed for “delivery of lecture” via the practice of teaching.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Mechanics of Polymer Solids and Fluids
courses.description: Continuum mechanics of solids and fluids; mechanics of deformation of anisotropic polymers; yield, breaking and fatigue; non-Newtonian vioscous and viscoelastic behavior of polymer fluids. Crosslisted with CHE, ME and PTFE 7771.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Fracture Mechanics
courses.description: Advanced study of failure of structural materials under load, mechanics of fracture, and microscopic and macroscopic aspects of the fracture of engineering materials. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and ME 7772.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fatigue of Materials and Structures
courses.description: Mechanical and microstructural aspects of nucleation and growth of cracks under cyclic loading conditions, notch effects, cumulative damage, multiaxial loading, and fatigue crack propagation. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and ME 7774.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Mechanics of Composites
courses.description: Anisotropic elasticity, hygrothermal behavior, stress analysis of laminated composites including 3-D effects, stress concentrations, free-edge effects, thick laminates, adhesive and mechanical connections, fracture of composites. Crosslisted with AE, CHE, CEE, ME, and PTFE 7792.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Manufacturing of Composites
courses.description: Major manufacturing techniques for metal, ceramic, and polymer composites. Modeling of processes with emphasis on fundamental mechanisms and effects. Crosslisted with AE, CHE, CEE, ME, and PTFE 7793.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: The latest advances in research and development will be presented by the enrolled students from articles in recent issues of recognized periodicals.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Presentation Skills
courses.description: Designing and explaining visuals; creating and delivering scientific electronic presentations; learning to speak and present to a variety of audiences.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topic offerings of current interest not included in regular courses.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topic offering of current interest not included in regular courses.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: special topics.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Special Problems
courses.description: Lectures, laboratory, and library work on special topics of current interest in materials suitable for a master's degree candidate.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Teaching Assistantship
courses.description: For graduate students holding teaching assistantships.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Research Assistantship
courses.description: For graduate students holding a research assistantship.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: GT-PKU
courses.description: For GT-PKU students during terms when they are not taking other GT courses. Placeholder course.
